payment_plan_downsell.name: Payment Plan Downsell (7-Step Framework)
payment_plan_downsell.summary: Offer the same product with flexible payment terms. Customers pay full price (or more) but with less upfront cost. Follow the 7-step framework from most profitable to least.
payment_plan_downsell.hormozi_principle: Always reward full payment first. Only move to payment plans after confirming they can't pay in full. The goal is to capture customers who would otherwise say no, not to cannibalize full-pay customers.

tasks.description: Always offer a discount for paying in full TODAY
tasks.script: 'If you can pay in full today, I can give you [X% off / bonus worth $X]. This is the best deal available.'
tasks.purpose: Captures maximum revenue from those who can pay

tasks.description: Offer external financing options (Affirm, Klarna, PayPal Credit, credit card)
tasks.script: 'No problem. Do you have a credit card with enough room, or would you like to use [financing option]?'
tasks.purpose: You get paid in full, they spread payments

tasks.description: Split payment into two: half today, half on next paycheck
tasks.script: 'What if we did half now ($X) and the other half in two weeks when you get paid?'
tasks.purpose: Low commitment to start, aligned with cash flow

tasks.description: Before going further, confirm they actually want it
tasks.script: 'On a scale of 1-10, how badly do you want this result? ... If it's 8+, let's figure out how to make this work. If it's 7 or below, maybe we should look at a different option.'
tasks.purpose: Don't waste time on low-desire prospects; consider feature downsell instead

tasks.description: Split into thirds: 1/3 today, 1/3 next paycheck, 1/3 after that
tasks.script: 'What if we did three payments of $X each? First one today, then aligned with your next two paychecks.'
tasks.timing: Schedule payments on their actual paycheck dates

tasks.description: Spread payments evenly across the program/service duration
tasks.script: 'What if we spread this across the full 16 weeks? That's just $X per week.'

tasks.description: Only as final option—free trial with completion requirements
tasks.script: 'Here's what I can do. You can start for free, but you need to [complete X actions]. If you do, you keep going free. If you don't, the card on file gets charged.'
tasks.link: See Trial With Penalty offer for full implementation

tasks.description: Ensure you can charge cards on schedule
Pre-built options for each step of the 7-step framework

tasks.task: Align payments with customer paycheck dates
tasks.description: Ask when they get paid and schedule around that
tasks.script: 'When do you typically get paid—1st and 15th, or every two weeks?'

tasks.description: Automatic retry and notification system for failed payments
Always attempt full payment and reward it before mentioning plans
tasks.critical: If full-pay rate drops, you're offering plans too early

tasks.description: Full payment should have clear advantages

tasks.task: Track full-pay vs. payment plan ratio
tasks.description: Monitor this closely—shouldn't shift dramatically
tasks.warning_sign: If payment plan % jumps significantly, you're cannibalizing

tasks.description: Confirm schedule, align with paycheck dates
Remind why they bought—reduce buyer's remorse
Help them get early result—increases completion

tasks.task: 2 days before each payment: Reminder + value
tasks.description: Remind payment coming, reinforce value received
When they finish paying, offer next tier

common_mistakes: Offering payment plans before attempting full payment
Not aligning payments with customer's paycheck schedule
Skipping the desire check (Step 4) and pushing low-desire prospects
Treating payment plan customers as less important
quick_wins: Start with Steps 1-3 only (simplest to implement)
Always ask 'When do you get paid?' for scheduling
Add 10-15% to payment plan total to incentivize full payment

trial_with_penalty.name: Trial With Penalty
trial_with_penalty.summary: Free trial where customers must meet requirements (show up, do homework, complete actions) or pay fees. Card on file FIRST, terms SECOND. Uses 'avoiding fees' as motivator.
trial_with_penalty.hormozi_principle: Get card FIRST, explain terms SECOND. 'That's just how we've always done it.' People avoid losing money (fees) more than they pursue gaining money (refunds).

tasks.task: Get card BEFORE explaining trial terms
tasks.description: Capture payment method first as 'account setup'
tasks.script: 'Great! Let me get your account set up. I'll need a card on file—that's just how we've always done it.'
tasks.key: Don't explain the trial until AFTER you have the card

tasks.task: Frame card capture as standard procedure
tasks.description: Make it feel routine, not suspicious
language: That's just how our system works...

tasks.description: After card captured, explain what they need to do
tasks.script: 'Perfect. Now here's how the trial works. As long as you [do X, Y, Z], it's completely free. Here's what that looks like...'

tasks.description: Explain how long it takes to hit their goal
tasks.script: 'Based on what you told me, realistically it takes X months to get [result]. So we ask for at least that commitment.'

tasks.description: Specific actions they must complete to stay free
Associate fees with NOT consuming, not with penalties
tasks.framing: 'These aren't penalties—they're accountability fees. If you do the work, you never pay them.'

tasks.description: Build in mandatory calls for upsell opportunities
tasks.purpose: Each check-in is an upsell opportunity

tasks.description: If they like it, upsell to paid
tasks.script: 'How's it going so far? Great! Since you're loving it, let me show you what the full program looks like and get your billing set up.'

tasks.description: If they hate it, diagnose why and offer better fit
tasks.script: 'I hear some frustration. Let me understand what's not working... Based on that, I think [different product] might actually be better for you. Want me to swap you over?'

tasks.description: If they didn't use it, re-engage or collect fees
sequence: Offer fee waiver if they return
If no response, charge accumulated fees

tasks.description: Track who's completing requirements and who's not
Nudge before they miss requirements
tasks.timing: 24 hours before deadline, 1 hour before deadline

tasks.description: How and when fees are charged to card on file
tasks.timing: Charge weekly or at end of trial based on accumulated fees

tasks.description: Seamless transition from trial to paying customer

tasks.task: Day 0: Welcome + how to stay free forever
tasks.description: Explain exactly what they need to do to never pay a fee
Push them to complete first requirement immediately
Help them see value fast so they WANT to upgrade
Show what they've completed and what's pending

tasks.task: End of trial: Conversion or fee collection
tasks.description: Convert to paid OR collect fees for non-compliance

common_mistakes: Explaining trial terms BEFORE getting card (kills conversion)
Making requirements too easy (no engagement = no conversion)
Making requirements too hard (frustration = bad reviews)
Not following up on non-compliant users
Forgetting to use check-ins as upsell opportunities
quick_wins: Script the card capture moment word-for-word
Start with 3 simple requirements (show up, do homework, check in)
Make first requirement completable within 24 hours

feature_downsell.name: Feature Downsell
feature_downsell.summary: Remove features from HIGHEST to LOWEST value so customers see what they're losing. They often 're-upsell' themselves when they realize the value of removed features.
feature_downsell.hormozi_principle: Remove highest-value features FIRST. After seeing the price difference, customers realize the value of what's removed and often add features back. You're helping them find the BEST DEAL, not the cheapest option.

tasks.task: List all features by value to customer
tasks.description: Rank features from most valuable to least valuable
tasks.format: Feature | Value to Customer | Cost to Deliver | Remove Order
tasks.principle: Remove highest-value features first so they feel the loss

tasks.task: Calculate price for each feature removal
tasks.description: Determine how much to reduce price when each feature is removed
tasks.approach: Price reduction should be LESS than perceived value of feature

tasks.description: Pre-built options at different price points
tasks.naming: Give each tier a name, not just a price

tasks.description: Know which features deliver which outcomes
tasks.use: Helps prescribe right tier for customer's goals

tasks.description: Show them what they'd lose and the new price
tasks.script: 'What if we removed [most valuable feature]? That brings the price down to $X. How does that feel?'

tasks.description: Let them process the loss of the feature
tasks.watch_for: Often they say 'Wait, I actually want that...' (re-upsell)

tasks.description: If still too expensive, remove next feature
tasks.script: 'Okay, if we also remove [next feature], we're at $X. Better?'

tasks.description: Check desire level (1-10) before continuing
tasks.script: 'On a scale of 1-10, how much do you want this result now? ... If 8+, let's keep finding the right fit. If 7 or below, maybe we should look at a payment plan instead.'

tasks.task: Step 5: Position as finding BEST DEAL
tasks.description: Frame yourself as helpful guide, not desperate salesperson
tasks.script: 'I want to find the best deal for YOU—not just the cheapest option. What matters most to you?'

tasks.task: Step 6: Combine with payment plan if needed
tasks.description: Once they like a feature combo, payment plan the price
tasks.script: 'Perfect. So you want [features X, Y, Z] at $X. What if we spread that over 3 payments?'

tasks.description: After they're engaged, offer to add back removed features
tasks.timing: 2-4 weeks into program when they see value
tasks.script: 'Now that you're seeing results, want to add [removed feature] to accelerate?'

tasks.description: Educate them on value of premium features
tasks.approach: Free orientation showing what premium features enable

tasks.description: When current customers try to cancel, feature downsell to retain
tasks.script: 'Before you cancel, what if we moved you to [lower tier] instead? You'd keep [core benefits] at a lower price.'
tasks.result: Often becomes 2nd highest LTV customer group

tasks.description: Visual showing what's included in each tier
Practice removing features in right order
Know which customers are on which tier for re-upsell
Intercept cancellations with downsell offer
Confirm their tier choice was the best deal for them
Prove the value of what they DID buy
Tease what premium features enable
Are they hitting limits? Ready for upgrade?
Offer to add back specific features they need

common_mistakes: Removing lowest-value features first (no pain = no re-upsell)
Not offering payment plans on downsold packages
quick_wins: Create just 3 tiers to start (Full, Standard, Basic)
Add cancellation flow that offers tier downgrade first
Train team to pause after removing each feature (let them feel the loss)
